solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Postpones advertisement about sending back unopened mail

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other, the advert wrapping the rest

parts.note: a puff is a promotional plug, a piece of advertising

indicators.note: sending back says the trimmed mail word is read in the opposite direction
unopened means the mail word loses its opening letter

parts.note: post is mail

explanation.surface: Someone delays acting on an advert, returning the post without opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unopened' and 'sending back' both act on the mail word, which then sits inside the advert; 'advertisement' is a puff, not an ad.
explanation.definitionFit: To put off a meeting is to delay it until later, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: With grand ceremony, order anti- aircraft gun

parts.note: pomp is splendid ceremonial display
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A gun is fired off with full military ceremony, by order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' only joins; 'order' is not a command but the Order of Merit, OM.
explanation.definitionFit: The pom-pom was a quick-firing gun used against planes in the Second World War.

clue.text: Round featuring hard key and time signature

indicators.note: featuring means the round contains the other pieces within it

parts.note: a tour is a round trip or circuit
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a key (cay) is a low island or reef

explanation.surface: A musical round written in a difficult key with a particular metre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks musical but is the island sense, a reef.
explanation.definitionFit: Three-four is the waltz metre, three crotchet beats to each bar.

clue.text: Don't start being mean and allow nestling

indicators.note: don't start says to drop the first letter of the word for mean

parts.note: low means base or mean
let means allow

explanation.surface: Advice not to begin being nasty and to let a chick be.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling is a young bird still in the nest, and a young owl is one example.

clue.text: Town open instead of shut, in the end

parts.note: frank means open or candid
for can mean in place of, as in swapping one for another

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of the word shut

explanation.surface: A town where everything is open rather than closed, at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Frankfort is the state capital of Kentucky, not to be confused with Frankfurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Frankfort is a small city, the capital of Kentucky in the United States.

clue.text: Pundit's article erased from history during row

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is just the pundit

indicators.note: during puts the trimmed history word in the middle of the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: erased from means the article is taken out of the history word

parts.note: the past is history
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A commentator's article is deleted from the record in the middle of a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but is a tier of seats; 'erased from' turns PAST into PST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster offers forecasts, such as racing tips, much as a pundit gives expert predictions.

clue.text: Put pressure on, say, for changes of direction

indicators.note: say signals that the word for putting pressure on is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain or burden them

explanation.surface: Someone puts pressure on another, perhaps to make them change course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing boat makes tacks, zigzag changes of course into the wind.

clue.text: In favour of controls over German spendthrifts

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the controls go round the German

parts.note: dials are controls on a device

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of German spendthrifts, approving of their control.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigals are people who waste money recklessly, as in the parable of the prodigal son.

clue.text: Musical figure not going through insignificant line

indicators.note: not going means the word for through is left out of the trivial word

parts.note: trivial means insignificant
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A musical phrase that doesn't pass through a minor line of the score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not going through' reads as one phrase, but 'through' is VIA, removed from TRIVIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A trill is an ornament of rapid alternation between two adjacent notes.

clue.text: Decorations essentially from opposing groups

indicators.note: essentially points to the core of the word from, its middle letters

parts.note: a set is a group

indicators.note: opposing means the second group faces the other way, read backwards

parts.note: a set is a group, here the second, facing group

explanation.surface: Rival factions each wear their own decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opposing groups' supplies two groups from one word, the second facing the first, so it is written backwards; 'essentially' takes the core of 'from'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosettes are ribbon badges awarded as prizes or worn as decorations by supporters.

clue.text: Extra-large mushroom

parts.note: more means extra
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An extra-large mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The morel is an edible fungus with a honeycombed cap, a kind of mushroom.

clue.text: Keeping his head, top-class corporal maybe competes for fish

parts.note: A, as in A1 or A-grade, means top class

indicators.note: keeping means the corporal holds the head of his inside

parts.note: a corporal is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of the word his

parts.note: vies means competes

explanation.surface: A cool-headed corporal of top quality competes for some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping his head' sounds like staying calm, but it puts the H of 'his' inside NCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anchovies are small, oily, strongly flavoured fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Finished with attempts to film passes

parts.note: over means finished
takes are attempts at filming a scene

explanation.surface: A film shoot is over after several attempts at a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that overtakes another passes it on the road.

clue.text: Small piece of land reverses direction to become small piece of water

indicators.note: reverses direction means the compass point south is replaced by north

parts.note: an islet is a tiny island

explanation.surface: A tiny island flips round and becomes a tiny patch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverses direction' does not turn the word round; it swaps S (south) for N (north).
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow arm of the sea or a lake running into the land.

clue.text: To give up somehow aroused me too

parts.note: to forgo is to give up or do without

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of aroused me are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: Someone told to give something up is somehow stirred as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' only joins; the definition is the last word, 'too'.
explanation.definitionFit: Done as an extra, or in addition, the idiom means much the same as also.

clue.text: Try doing the exercise when lacking energy — I'm off!

parts.note: a go is a try

indicators.note: to exercise is to work over, so the remaining letters are worked into a new order
lacking means the energy letter is dropped from the fodder

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone told to try the workout, low on energy, decides to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking energy' drops E from DOING THE, and 'exercise' rearranges DOINGTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying good night is a farewell at bedtime, announcing that you are leaving.

clue.text: Spread more salt at beginning of major turbulence

indicators.note: beginning of points to the first letter of the word major
spread means the letters of more salt are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Spreading extra salt at the start of a major storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' places the first letter of 'major' in front of the rearranged MORESALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively any state of turmoil.

clue.text: Physically assaulted old policemen

parts.note: used means second-hand, not new
the force is the police

explanation.surface: Former police officers attacked someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To use force on someone is to apply violence to them, an idiom for assault.

clue.text: Materials keep on going into films

indicators.note: going into puts the word for keeping on inside the films

parts.note: pics is informal for films
to last is to keep on or endure

explanation.surface: Materials that keep being used in films.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastics are synthetic substances moulded into products, a class of materials.

clue.text: Prince Charles frantically rifles toolshed

indicators.note: frantically means in a wild hurry, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: The heir to the throne searches wildly through his garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord of the Isles is a Scottish title held by the heir to the British throne, as Charles was then.
explanation.definitionFit: Among his many titles, the then Prince of Wales was styled with this old Scottish dignity.

clue.text: Lose clothes in county drains

indicators.note: in places the outside letters inside the county

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: clothes means the outer covering of the word Lose, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A command to strip off somewhere in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothes' is a noun: the outside of 'Lose', L and E. BEDS is Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleed something is to drain liquid or air from it, as with a radiator.

clue.text: Singular man's offspring

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a pawn is a chess man

explanation.surface: One particular man's children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a chess piece, the pawn; the 's only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Spawn means offspring, originally the eggs of fish or frogs, used loosely of children.

clue.text: Be sick about voting system which takes 30 days

indicators.note: about means the illness word goes round the voting system

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell
PR is proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: Feeling ill about an electoral system that drags on for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the rhyme 'Thirty days hath September, April, June and November'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth month of the year has thirty days, as the old calendar rhyme reminds us.

clue.text: Arrogant graduates crying when one goes missing

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, graduates

indicators.note: goes missing means the one letter is dropped from the crying word

parts.note: tearful means crying
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Haughty graduates weep when one of their number vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone masterful is domineering and imperious, overbearing in manner.

clue.text: Spots infiltrators

definitions.meaning: skin blemishes or small dark marks on the body

explanation.definitionFit: Moles are both dark marks on skin and double agents placed inside a rival organisation.

clue.text: Cargo abandoned by French crew

indicators.note: abandoned by means the French abbreviation leaves the cargo word

parts.note: freight is cargo

explanation.surface: A French crew leaves its cargo behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew' is a rowing boat's team of oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing eight is a boat crewed by eight oarsmen, plus a cox.

clue.text: Extraordinary Irish piece returned by retired artist

indicators.note: returned means the pistol word is read backwards

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun, such as a Luger pistol

indicators.note: retired means the artist abbreviation is turned back to front

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A remarkable Irish painting sent back by an artist who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' suggests a work of art, but it is a gun, the Luger.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular can mean out of the ordinary, departing from normal rules or patterns.

clue.text: Little bit of string wound around prickly plant

indicators.note: around means the wound word encloses the little bit of string

parts.note: to gore is to wound with a horn

indicators.note: little bit of points to just the first letter of the word string

explanation.surface: A short length of string wrapped round a thorny bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like the past of wind, but it is the verb meaning injure: GORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorse, or furze, is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths.

clue.text: Playing back stringed instruments shows respect for rank

indicators.note: back means the playing word is read the other way

parts.note: as can mean playing the part of, as in an actor credited as Hamlet
lutes are stringed instruments

explanation.surface: Musicians replaying stringed instruments to honour a senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier salutes a superior officer as a formal mark of respect for seniority.

clue.text: Parents mark the rest

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
the others are the rest

explanation.surface: Parents grade everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Mothers are female parents, so the definition is a broader term for them.
